principles.statement: A field that is mutated through a write path but only ever stored in an in-process cache — never actually serialized into the durable storage format — will silently reset to empty/default on every process restart, with no error, warning, or visible symptom until something downstream depends on it being populated.
principles.rationale: Confirmed live 2026-09-15: ZSEI's ContainerStorage kept `GlobalState.child_ids` (a variable-length list) solely in an in-memory `child_ids_cache: HashMap`, populated only by this process's own `store()` calls, while the fixed-width mmap header only ever persisted `container_id`/`child_count`/`version`/`parent_id`. Every restart silently reset every container's child_ids to empty. Nothing crashed or logged an error — the system just quietly behaved as if no children existed until this session's own writes rebuilt part of the picture.

principles.statement: When a storage format has both a durable representation (disk/mmap) and a derived in-memory structure, verify at review time that the in-memory structure is actually reconstructed FROM the durable representation on load — not just populated forward from future writes.
principles.rationale: The asymmetry is easy to miss because the write path looks completely correct in isolation (store() does update child_ids_cache) — the bug only exists in the gap between 'what gets written' and 'what gets read back after a restart', which a write-path-only review will never surface.

heuristics.name: Ask 'Does This Survive a Restart' For Every Cache
heuristics.description: For any HashMap/cache field alongside a durable store, explicitly ask: if the process restarted right now with zero in-memory state, would this field be correctly repopulated from disk alone? If the honest answer is 'only partially, from whatever this session happens to create fresh,' that is a real, live bug, not a performance nuance.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Reviewing or writing any storage layer that combines a durable on-disk format with an in-memory cache/index structure.
examples: child_ids_cache in src/zsei/storage.rs looked completely correct from its write side (store() always updated it) but was never rebuilt from the durable parent_id links already persisted per-container — confirmed by asking exactly this question during an unrelated post-restart investigation.

heuristics.name: Derive What's Missing From What's Actually Persisted
heuristics.description: When a derived field can't be stored directly in a fixed-format record (e.g. a variable-length list in a fixed-width binary header), check whether it can be reconstructed on load from OTHER fields that ARE correctly persisted, rather than requiring a storage-format rewrite.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Fixing a missing-on-reload field where a full storage-format change would be high-risk or out of scope.
examples: child_ids couldn't fit the fixed 64-byte header record, but parent_id (which every child already persists about itself) could be reverse-indexed at boot into a correct child_ids_cache with one cheap extra pass over already-loaded containers — no format change needed.

decision_rules.condition: A field lives in both a durable store and an in-memory cache/index, and something downstream (an idempotency check, a traversal, a count) depends on that field being accurate immediately after a restart.
decision_rules.action: Verify with a real restart test (not just a read of the write-path code) that the field is correctly non-empty for pre-existing data on the very first read after the process comes back up.
exceptions: The field is explicitly documented and intended as session-scoped/ephemeral (e.g. a request-rate counter), not something meant to reflect durable state.
